video_title: Micah Nori Postgame Interview | Trail Blazers 123, Oklahoma City Thunder 103 | Nov. 10, 2026

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the keys to the Trail Blazers' victory
quotes.excerpt: at the end of the day you got to take care of the basketball
quotes.quote: Like we talked about at the very beginning of the night, against these guys, I've seen enough, not my first rodeo. I mean, at the end of the day you got to take care of the basketball. We only had nine turnovers, they had 12, and the offensive rebounds were the same. And the other reason we won is because we were 24 for 26 from the free throw line.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori credits the Trail Blazers win over OKC to taking care of the basketball and hitting free throws, noting the team finished 24 for 26 from the line.

structured.context: Micah Nori discusses the keys to the Trail Blazers victory over the Oklahoma City Thunder.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on adjusting to Damian Lillard's scoring outbursts
quotes.excerpt: it's a lot more fun on this side of it
quotes.quote: Basically the Phoenix game was the first time I saw it, and it's a lot more fun on this side of it. I really think, to your point, we took control of the game, but I think those last two little flurries, the Deni three at the end of the third and obviously Damian's to extend it a little bit, kind of put it away, if you will.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says it is a lot more fun being on the same side as Damian Lillard during his scoring outbursts, noting that late flurries from Lillard and Deni Avdija helped put the game away.

structured.context: Micah Nori reflects on the late game scoring flurries from Deni Avdija and Damian Lillard.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on Chris Youngblood's impact off the bench
quotes.excerpt: the moment's not too big for him
quotes.quote: He's been phenomenal. I think the one thing that I like about Chris Youngblood is that the moment's not too big for him. I didn't even really plan on him playing in the Denver game until Vlatko got the three fouls and he just came off the bench and he was a plus 15 in that half. Not afraid of the moment, he competes, he defends, and he can make a shot.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori praises Chris Youngblood for his impact off the bench, saying the moment is not too big for him and highlighting his ability to compete, defend, and make shots.

structured.context: Micah Nori praises Chris Youngblood for his performance off the bench against the Denver Nuggets.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the decision to change the starting lineup
quotes.excerpt: I wanted to get Scoot with the second unit again
quotes.quote: My thought process was that I wanted to get Scoot with the second unit again because I just felt like with Deni and with Damian with that first group, those guys were taking the majority of the handling of the basketball. And I wanted to get Scoot with that second unit. It also allowed me to clean up where I got Damian back to playing what he's used to his whole career, which is two stints and a half instead of three.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori explains the decision to move Scoot Henderson to the second unit, aiming to give him more ball-handling opportunities while returning Damian Lillard to his traditional rotation.

structured.context: Micah Nori explains the strategic decision to move Scoot Henderson to the second unit.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the team's defensive effort against Oklahoma City
quotes.excerpt: it feels like a death by a thousand cuts when he's making them
quotes.quote: It was very good. And I think the one thing that Oklahoma City does is they take a lot of mid-range shots. It's funny because you don't want to give up rim and you don't want to give up threes, but then Shai comes in and I think probably shoots the mid-range 52, 54 percent the way he's shooting it. So it kind of feels like a death by a thousand cuts when he's making them. But I thought the defense did a very good job.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori breaks down the defensive strategy against Oklahoma City, noting the difficulty of defending Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's mid-range game.

structured.context: Micah Nori evaluates the team's defensive performance against Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the Thunder.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on Scoot Henderson's role and team fit
quotes.excerpt: Scoot's going to help us win a lot of basketball games this year
quotes.quote: I honestly believe that he is better for us with that second unit when we can have him initiate and do some things there. And I feel like he just kind of gets lost a little bit with that first group. And with Damian and Deni having the ball so much, it works out perfectly to have another defender out there with a little more size and then get Scoot. And it also lets him run a little more consistent minutes. Scoot's going to help us win a lot of basketball games this year. I believe in Scoot Henderson. I honestly do.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori doubles down on his belief in Scoot Henderson, stating he is better suited for the second unit where he can initiate the offense and get more consistent minutes.

structured.context: Micah Nori elaborates on why Scoot Henderson fits better with the second unit.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on Chris Youngblood's foot injury
quotes.excerpt: I noticed him limping after the breakaway
quotes.quote: I think that it looked like when he got the steal, and it looked like when he went to go finish whether he stepped awkwardly. So they're going to check him out and see what's happened. But then I just saw him limping a little bit and that's why he really didn't say take me out, but you could tell something was wrong. But I noticed him limping after the breakaway and then on the one finish it looked like I think he just either stepped awkwardly or whatnot. So hopefully he'll be okay.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says Chris Youngblood is being evaluated for a foot injury after appearing to limp following a breakaway finish against the Thunder.

structured.context: Micah Nori provides an update on Chris Youngblood after he appeared to suffer a foot injury.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the team's collective effort and chemistry
quotes.excerpt: when your heart is pure, your heart's in the right place, it's funny how good things happen
quotes.quote: When Donovan picked up his third foul in the first half and I could have gone back, Rob, very easily. But there's something about playing against your old team. And Brandon Carlson being a former Thunder and went in, got a big putback and ends up with five rebounds in almost eight minutes, but and blocks two shots. So I thought that it was really cool to see him. And I think that what's great about this team is, you've seen Michael Porter do that in moments, you've seen Hansen do that, you've seen Brandon. We already spoke about Chris Youngblood. It's just, when your heart is pure, your heart's in the right place, it's funny how good things happen for you. And quite honestly, that locker room, that's the way they all are.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori praises the depth and chemistry of the Trail Blazers, noting that different players are stepping up when called upon because their hearts are in the right place.

structured.context: Micah Nori discusses the team's chemistry and the contributions of various players off the bench.
